# ci-manager-local

**Make declared resources exist on this machine, and record what it made.**

A forge-ci `manager` engine.

## Why it exists

It creates directories and files. Nothing else. That is the point: a manager
you can run with no cloud and no credential, so the seam between engines and
managers is testable on a laptop.

## Tools

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `reconcile` | Realize every declared resource and return who owns it. |

## By hand

```sh
echo '{"manager":"local","resources":[{"kind":"directory","name":"/tmp/state"}]}' \
  | ci-manager-local reconcile
```

## In a pipeline

```yaml
engines:
  - alias: my-manager
    type: manager
    engine: "forge://github.com/alexandremahdhaoui/forge-ci/cmd/ci-manager-local@v0.1.4"
    manager: local
    spec:
      statePath: <string>
```

## Worth knowing

It knows `directory` and `file`. An existing file is kept, never overwritten.
Anything else is refused by name.

It refuses outright when a resource is recorded as owned by a different manager.
It never creates a second copy beside the first.
